kort.s: I have a thousand needles but never sew a stitch. In December I stand all dressed up in the living room. What am I?
kort.f: Fir trees have needles – and become Christmas trees.

kort.s: I carry my house on my back and move so slowly you could wave at me for an hour. Who am I?
kort.f: A snail takes its shell everywhere.

kort.s: I have a cap but no head, and I pop up in the woods after the rain. What am I?
kort.f: A mushroom has a cap and a stalk.

kort.s: I have eyes but can't see a thing. You boil me and mash me for tea. What am I?
kort.f: The little dots on a potato are called eyes.

kort.s: I'm black and white, striped like a zebra crossing, and I live on the savannah. Who am I?
I start as a tadpole in the pond and hop onto land when I'm grown up. Who am I?
I'm round and orange, and at Halloween I get a face and a candle inside me. What am I?
I have six sides covered in spots, and I tumble across the table when it's your turn to move. What am I?
I have a long neck, patches all over, and I eat leaves from the tops of trees. Who am I?
I'm brown in summer and white in winter, and I have very long ears. Who am I?
kort.f: Mountain hares change their coat to hide in the snow.

kort.s: You can't see me, but you can hear me in the trees and feel me in your hair. What am I?
I follow you around when the sun shines, but vanish when the clouds come. What am I?
I'm full of holes but still soak up water, and you wash with me in the bath. What am I?
My nose is longer than your arms, and I use it to have a shower. Who am I?
I have whiskers but I'm not a grandad. I say miaow when I want my tea. Who am I?
I have lots of colours but no paintbrush. I appear when the sun and the rain meet. What am I?
I live in a hive and work all summer to make something sweet. Who am I?
kort.f: Bees make honey.

kort.s: I'm hard and yellow in the packet, but I go white and fluffy when I pop in the pan. What am I?
I often stand on one leg, and I'm pink because I eat tiny shrimps. Who am I?
kort.f: Its colour comes from its food.

kort.s: I have a shell and claws, and I walk sideways along the beach. Who am I?
I have three lights but I'm not a lamp. When I turn green, the cars can go. What am I?
I'm a house made of snow blocks, and you can crawl inside me. What am I?
I'm empty on the way to the shop and full on the way home. What am I?
I have a hump on my back and can walk a long way through the desert without a drink. Who am I?
I'm green when I'm young and yellow when I'm ripe, and you peel me before you eat me. What am I?
You toss me in the air when you can't agree, and shout ‘heads’ or ‘tails’. What am I?
I have eight arms and squirt ink when I'm frightened. Who am I?
I'm as white as the snow, I live in the far north and I swim in the freezing sea. Who am I?
I come out at night and leave in the morning, and some nights I'm perfectly round. What am I?
I have a long tail and love cheese, but the cat is not my friend. Who am I?
I'm round and sweet with a hole in the middle, and lovely dunked in hot chocolate. What am I?
I have wings but no feathers, and I can fly you off on your summer holiday. What am I?
I run on rails and hoot as I go into the tunnel. What am I?
I have a shell on my back, I'm no knight, and some of us live for over a hundred years. Who am I?
I'm made from milk and full of holes, but nothing ever leaks out of me. What am I?
I have a beak, I swim on the pond, and my babies follow me in a line. Who am I?
I grow under the ground, I'm orange, and rabbits love me. What am I?
I get smaller every time you fix a mistake, but I never complain. What am I?
kort.f: In Britain an eraser is a rubber.

kort.s: I get shorter every time you sharpen me. What am I?
I wear lots of layers, and you cry when you take them off. What am I?
kort.f: Cutting an onion makes your eyes water.

kort.s: I drink with my feet and turn my face to the sun all day. What am I?
I sleep upside down all day, and at night I fly out to catch insects. Who am I?
I have a pocket on my tummy and hop instead of walking. Who am I?
I'm green and covered in spikes, and I can go a long time without rain in the desert. What am I?
I open up when it rains and wait by the front door when it's sunny. What am I?
I have a door and a light, and inside me it's cold all year round. What am I?
I have a tail and fly high over the park when it's windy, but I'm not a bird. What am I?
I have four legs and a back, but I never get backache. What am I?
I swap a baby tooth for a coin while you're asleep. Who am I?
I'm covered in prickles and curl up into a ball when I'm scared. Who am I?
I have feathers but can't fly. I swim in icy seas and look as if I'm wearing a suit. Who am I?
I swallow you up in the morning and let you out again after school. What am I?
I have no feet, but I run into the sink when you turn me on. What am I?
I twinkle high up at night, and you can make a wish when one of us falls. What am I?
I'm water that has frozen, and I clink in your glass when you pour squash over me. What am I?
I have one eye but can't see, and I pull thread through cloth. What am I?
I have two wheels and pedals but no engine, and I fall over if you stop pedalling. What am I?
I sleep all winter in a den and wake up hungry in spring. Who am I?
I have eight legs, I spin a web and I catch flies. Who am I?
I get big and round when you blow into me, and I go bang if you squeeze too hard. What am I?
I stand outside all winter with a carrot for a nose, and I cry when spring arrives. Who am I?
kort.f: When it warms up, the snowman melts.

kort.s: I'm green, I jump about in the grass and I make music with my legs. Who am I?
kort.f: Grasshoppers rub their legs on their wings to chirp.

kort.s: I go up and down without moving an inch. What am I?
I have a thousand tiny hairs on my head and work in your mouth morning and night. What am I?
I have wheels and a hood, and I push teddies round the living room. What am I?
I have lots of buttons but no shirt. You press me to change the channel. What am I?
I'm made of paper, full of stories, and I live on a shelf. What am I?
I'm white and hard and I live in your mouth. You brush me every night. What am I?
I'm red and round and hang on a tree in autumn. What am I?
I have big eyes, I say ‘twit-twoo’ and I hunt at night. Who am I?
I'm the biggest animal in the sea, and I blow water out of a hole on my head. Who am I?
I'm cold, white and sweet, and I melt in the sun on top of a cone. What am I?
I have a nose that sniffs and a tail that wags. Who am I?
Inside me are rings that tell you how old I am. What am I?
kort.f: A tree grows a new ring every year.

kort.s: I'm woolly and white and I say ‘baa’. Who am I?
I'm small and yellow, I say ‘cheep’ and I've just hatched from an egg. Who am I?
I'm white and cold, and I float down in winter without making a sound. What am I?
I have four wheels and a siren, and I drive fast when someone needs help. What am I?
A shepherd has 12 goats. All but 5 jump over the fence. How many are left?
kort.f: ‘All but five’ means five stay behind.

kort.s: Which is heavier: ten kilos of popcorn or ten kilos of nails?
kort.f: Ten kilos is ten kilos.

kort.s: An electric car drives west in a howling gale. Which way does the exhaust blow?
kort.f: Electric cars have no exhaust.

kort.s: How many times can you take 5 away from 50?
kort.f: After that you're taking it away from 45.

kort.s: Oliver's mum has three children: Spring, Summer and …?
kort.f: Oliver is the third child.

kort.s: Which word gets shorter when you add two letters to it?
kort.f: Short becomes shorter.

kort.s: What can you touch with your right hand but never with your left?
kort.f: Try touching your right elbow with your right hand …

kort.s: Before Mount Everest was discovered, what was the highest mountain in the world?
kort.f: It was just as high before anyone found it.

kort.s: How much soil is in a hole one metre deep and one metre wide?
kort.f: A hole is empty.

kort.s: What has a neck but no head, and two arms but no hands?
Which months have a 28th day?
kort.f: Every month has at least 28 days.

kort.s: Can a kangaroo jump higher than a house?
kort.f: Houses can't jump at all.

kort.s: What goes up every year but never comes down?
What belongs to you but is used more by other people?
You're running a race and overtake the person in second place. What place are you in now?
kort.f: You took their place.

kort.s: Is there a 5th of November in France?
kort.f: Every year – they just don't have bonfires.

kort.s: Which letter can you drink?
kort.f: Tea!

kort.s: Which letter is a body of water?
kort.f: Sea!

kort.s: Which letter is a buzzing insect?
kort.f: Bee!

kort.s: Which letter grows in a pod?
kort.f: Pea!

kort.s: Which letter is a bird?
kort.f: A jay is a bird.

kort.s: Which letter asks a question?
kort.f: Why?

kort.s: How many apples grow on a pine tree?
kort.f: Apples grow on apple trees.

kort.s: How many letters are there in ‘the alphabet’?
kort.f: T-h-e-a-l-p-h-a-b-e-t.

kort.s: What's in the middle of Leeds?
kort.f: L-e-e-d-s.

kort.s: Which word is always spelled wrong in the dictionary?
kort.f: The word ‘wrong’ – spelled perfectly.

kort.s: What goes all the way round the garden without moving an inch?
When can you drop an egg on a concrete floor without cracking it?
kort.f: Concrete floors are very hard to crack.

kort.s: What's black when you buy it, red when you use it and grey when you throw it away?
What has teeth but never eats, and keeps your coat done up?
What has a head and a foot but no body – and you sleep in it?
What has arms but no hands, and sits in the living room?
What has legs but never goes anywhere, and you eat your tea at it?
What goes on four legs in the morning, two legs at midday and three legs in the evening?
kort.f: A baby crawls, a grown-up walks and an old person uses a stick. The Sphinx's own riddle!

kort.s: Which week of the year is the shortest?
kort.f: Every week has seven days.

kort.s: What has four wheels and flies?
Who wears iron shoes but has never been to a shoe shop?
kort.f: Horses wear horseshoes.

kort.s: What has a neck but no head, and a cork instead of a hat?
What has lots of teeth but never goes to the dentist?
What has to be broken before you can use it?
What goes through glass without breaking it?
The more of me there is, the less you see. What am I?
Say my name and I'm gone. What am I?
What can you hear but never see, and only answers when you shout?
What can travel round the world while staying in the corner of an envelope?
I have towns without houses, forests without trees and rivers without water. What am I?
Which number gets smaller when you turn it upside down?
kort.f: Turn 9 upside down and you get 6.

kort.s: Where does Friday come before Monday?
kort.f: F comes before M in the alphabet.

kort.s: What's always in front of you but can never be seen?
How much water is there in an empty bucket?
kort.f: As soon as there's water in it, it isn't empty any more.

kort.s: What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
Which tree can you hold in your hand?
kort.f: A palm tree – and the palm of your hand.

kort.s: What do you call a bear with no teeth?
What do a needle, a storm and a potato all have?
kort.f: The eye of a needle, the eye of a storm and a potato's eyes.

kort.s: What do a book, a hedgehog and a cactus all have?
What do a bottle, a guitar and a giraffe all have?
What do a saw, a zip and a crocodile all have?
What do a tree and a dog both have?
What do an elephant, a tree and an old travelling chest all have?
What do a cricket match and a dark cave both have?
What do a telephone, a boxing match and your finger all have?
What do a shoe and your mouth both have?
What do a clock and you both have?
What do a river and your bedroom both have?
What do a pack of cards and you both have?
What do a king and a tooth both have?
What do a mountain and a sock both have?
What animal lives next to the computer?
What kind of room has no doors and no windows?
What has lots of keys but can't open a single lock?
What can you catch but never throw?
What can you break without even touching it?
What's at the end of a rainbow?
kort.f: The last letter of ‘rainbow’.

kort.s: Grandad goes out in the pouring rain without an umbrella, hat or hood. His clothes are soaked, but not a single hair gets wet. How?
A train one kilometre long goes through a tunnel one kilometre long, at one kilometre a minute. How long until the whole train is out?
kort.f: The front has to travel two kilometres before the last carriage is out.

kort.s: You have one match and walk into a dark cottage with a candle, an oil lamp and a wood burner. What do you light first?
A farmer has three haystacks in one corner of a field and five in another. He puts them all together. How many haystacks does he have now?
kort.f: They've become one big haystack.

kort.s: A window cleaner falls off his ladder by a twenty-storey building but isn't hurt. How?
kort.a: He was on the bottom rung

kort.s: You're in a race and overtake the person in last place. What place are you in?
kort.f: Nobody can overtake the last person – you'd have to be behind them.

kort.s: Two fathers and two sons go fishing. They catch three fish, and each gets one. How?
kort.f: The dad is both a father and a son.

kort.s: A mum has seven daughters, and each daughter has one brother. How many children does she have?
kort.f: All seven share the same brother.

kort.s: Which number comes after 1, 4, 9, 16, 25?
Which number is missing: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, …?
kort.f: Prime numbers: they can only be divided by 1 and themselves.

kort.s: Which letter comes next: J, F, M, A, M, J, J, A, S, O, N?
kort.f: The first letters of the months – December is last.

kort.s: Which letter comes next: M, T, W, T, F, S?
kort.f: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday – Sunday!

kort.s: Which letter comes next: O, T, T, F, F, S, S?
kort.f: One, two, three, four, five, six, seven – eight!

kort.s: The doctor gives you three pills and says take one every half hour. How long until you've taken them all?
kort.f: One now, one after half an hour, one after an hour.

kort.s: It's exactly three o'clock. What's the angle between the hands?
kort.f: A quarter turn – a right angle.

kort.s: How can you throw a ball so it comes back to you without hitting anything?
A football match ended 3–2, but no men scored. How?
A dog is tied to a three-metre rope, yet it reaches a bone ten metres away. How?
kort.a: The rope isn't tied to anything

kort.s: There are three apples on the table. You take two. How many apples do you have?
kort.f: The two you took.

kort.s: How many months have 31 days?
kort.f: January, March, May, July, August, October and December.

kort.s: A lorry is stuck under a bridge – it's two centimetres too tall. How does it get free?
kort.a: Let some air out of the tyres

kort.s: A driver goes the wrong way down a one-way street. A police officer sees him but does nothing. Why?
What can fill a whole room without taking up any space?
A cook has two egg timers: one for 7 minutes and one for 11. How does she time exactly 15 minutes?
kort.a: Start both, then turn the 11 over when it runs out
kort.f: When the 7 runs out she starts cooking – 4 minutes left on the 11. When that runs out, turn it over: 4 + 11 = 15.

kort.s: You have 9 identical marbles, and one is slightly heavier. How few weighings on a balance do you need to find it?
kort.f: Weigh three against three – then one against one from the heavier group.

kort.s: What's half of a quarter of 80?
What comes next: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …?
kort.f: Each number is the sum of the two before it.

kort.s: How many holes does a T-shirt have?
kort.f: One for your head, two for your arms and one at the bottom.

kort.s: Yesterday was Sunday. What day comes after the day after tomorrow?
kort.f: Today is Monday, the day after tomorrow is Wednesday.

kort.s: How many times do you write the digit 1 when you write all the numbers from 1 to 20?
kort.f: 1, 10, 11 (twice) and 12 to 19.

kort.s: Which is right: ‘seven plus five is eleven’ or ‘seven plus five are eleven’?
kort.f: Seven plus five is twelve.

kort.s: Name three days in a row without saying Monday, Wednesday or Friday.
I'm a number. Multiply me by myself and I become four times bigger. What number am I?
kort.f: 4 × 4 = 16, and 16 is four times 4.

kort.s: A pig weighs 20 kilos plus half its own weight. How much does the pig weigh?
kort.f: Half is 20 kilos, so the whole pig is 40.

kort.s: A man looks at a photo and says: ‘Brothers and sisters I have none, but this man's father is my father's son.’ Who's in the photo?
kort.f: ‘My father's son’ is himself.

kort.s: How can you stand behind your dad while he stands behind you?
You have two coins that make 15p, and one of them isn't a 5p. What are they?
kort.f: One isn't a 5p – but the other one is.

kort.s: The bus driver has a brother, but the brother has no brother. How?
kort.a: The bus driver is his sister

kort.s: You have a basket with five apples and five children. How can each child get one apple and one still be left in the basket?
kort.a: The last child gets the basket with the apple in it

kort.s: A carpenter cuts a plank into ten pieces. Each cut takes one minute. How long does it take?
kort.f: Nine cuts make ten pieces.

kort.s: Three cats catch three mice in three minutes. How many cats do you need to catch a hundred mice in a hundred minutes?
kort.f: Together three cats catch one mouse a minute – a hundred in a hundred minutes.

kort.s: What do you get more of the more you take?
kort.f: The more steps you take, the more you've walked.

kort.s: You're the captain of a ship carrying 20 cows, 30 sheep and 10 goats. How old is the captain?
kort.f: You were the captain!

kort.s: What can you keep without ever touching it?
What's as big as an elephant but weighs nothing at all?
A girl has as many brothers as sisters, but each brother has twice as many sisters as brothers. How many children are in the family?
kort.f: Four girls and three boys.

kort.s: How do you share 7 apples equally between 12 children without cutting any apple into more than four pieces?
kort.a: Cut four apples into thirds and three into quarters
kort.f: Everyone gets one third and one quarter.

kort.s: A car goes at 60 kilometres an hour. How far does it go in 20 minutes?
A man buys a horse for £600, sells it for £700, buys it back for £800 and sells it again for £900. How much does he make?
kort.f: He makes £100 on each sale.

kort.s: How can two people stand on the same newspaper without being able to touch each other?
kort.a: Put the paper under a door
kort.f: One stands on each side of the door.

kort.s: What has twelve arms and hangs from the ceiling, but can't give hugs?
How many ends do three and a half sticks have?
kort.f: Half a stick still has two ends.

kort.s: There's a cat in each corner of a room. In front of each cat sit three cats. How many cats are there?
How many times does the minute hand go round in a day?
kort.f: Once an hour.

kort.s: What do you get if you multiply all the digits from 0 to 9 together?
kort.f: Anything times nought is nought.

kort.s: What's half of two plus two?
kort.f: Half of two is one – plus two makes three.

kort.s: How many times do you write the digit 9 when you write all the numbers from 1 to 100?
kort.f: Ten times in the units and ten times in the nineties.

kort.s: A bottle and a cork cost £1.10 together. The bottle costs £1 more than the cork. How much is the cork?
kort.f: The cork is 5p and the bottle £1.05 – £1.10 in all.

kort.s: Five machines make five toys in five minutes. How long do a hundred machines take to make a hundred toys?
Water lilies on a pond double every day. On day 30 they cover the whole pond. When did they cover half?
It's pitch dark, and a drawer is full of red and blue socks. How many do you need to take to be sure of a pair?
kort.f: With three socks, at least two must match.

kort.s: What comes after 2, 4, 8, 16, …?
kort.f: Each number doubles.

kort.s: A snail climbs a 10-metre well. It climbs 3 metres a day and slips 2 metres back at night. How many days does it take?
kort.f: After seven days and nights it's at 7 metres – on the eighth day it reaches the top.

kort.s: Kate is older than Sam. Sam is older than Lily. Who is youngest?
Two painters paint two houses in two days. How many houses do four painters paint in four days?
You're in a sinking boat with sharks circling. How do you save yourself?
kort.f: It was only something you were imagining.

kort.s: What can you put in a barrel to make it lighter?
How many sides does a circle have?
kort.f: The inside and the outside.

kort.s: When does 9 plus 5 equal 2?
kort.f: Nine o'clock plus five hours is two o'clock.

kort.s: How do you write twelve with just three symbols – and no digits?
kort.f: Roman numerals!

kort.s: How can half of 8 be 0?
kort.f: The top half of an 8 looks like a 0.
